value.rationale: With a fixed mean probe spacing, the previously studied quantum Zeno first-detection problem has a natural operational budget. The new sharp classification reveals an unattained frequent-probe plateau (randomized bursts), a unique deterministic middle regime, and an exactly characterizable long-budget resonant-mixture phase. These are structural transitions and complete optimizer support laws, not just a numerical improvement or the earlier unconstrained optimum. The closure versus positive-wait distinction is scientifically material; minimum-gap or cost-constrained variants remain open.
